articles.headline: [WAY – Waystar] Healthcare is a very complicated invoice
articles.summary: Scuttleblurb provides a deep-dive into Waystar (WAY), examining the extraordinary complexity of US healthcare billing — where ~18% of claims are initially denied, procedures carry dozens of different prices across payers, and administrative costs consume 15-25% of total healthcare spend. The piece dissects how Waystar's clearinghouse network and AI-powered denial management tools sit at the center of the claim-to-cash (RCM) workflow, processing a data-rich, high-stakes process that creates meaningful switching costs. The analysis frames Waystar's competitive moat as a function of network effects, workflow embeddedness, and the structural intractability of the billing problem itself.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors, this is the definitive independent moat assessment of WAY at a pivotal moment in the AI-RCM narrative, offering actionable insight into whether Waystar's competitive position is durable or vulnerable to disruption.

articles.headline: Bypassing RevenueBench to Buy the Feedback Loop
articles.summary: MBI Deep Dives introduces 'RevenueBench' as the emerging true benchmark for AI model quality — real-world wallet share — while arguing traditional benchmarks are becoming noisy and saturated. Meta is deliberately bypassing RevenueBench by giving away its latest models free in exchange for developer training data, rapidly capturing ~40% of tokens on OpenCode (5 trillion tokens/day), approaching twice Google's internal coding harness volume. This feedback loop strategy lets Meta compound model quality without charging for it, while also reducing its ~$10B annual spend on Anthropic and OpenAI APIs.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors, this reframes the AI competitive moat question away from benchmark performance toward data flywheel accumulation — with direct implications for Meta's long-term AI cost structure, Anthropic's revenue durability, and the viability of frontier model pricing power.
